notes.heading: Negation, elision and agreement with coordinated subjects
paragraphs: In standard written French, ne and pas normally surround the conjugated verb. Before a vowel sound or mute h, ne becomes n'; je also becomes j' before the relevant vowel sound. Elision changes spelling, not the subject or the verb ending. Two named people joined by et take a plural verb. A subject containing moi normally corresponds to nous, while a group containing toi but not moi corresponds to vous. In these exercises the verbs are regular -er verbs; do not extend their endings to every verb family.

questions.prompt: Rewrite 'J'aime le chocolat' as a standard written negative and explain the spelling of the negative particle.
solution: Place the negative pair around aime.
Use n' before aime; je is no longer directly before the vowel.
markingPoints: Write Je n'aime pas le chocolat.

questions.prompt: Complete 'Lina et moi ___ le français' with étudier in the present, then replace the subject with a pronoun.
questions.answer: Lina et moi étudions le français. Nous étudions le français.
solution: Lina et moi includes the speaker, so it corresponds to nous.
Use the nous ending -ons on the stem étudi-.

questions.prompt: Answer in French: 'Est-ce que vous parlez espagnol ?' Say that you speak French but do not speak Spanish, using je and standard written negation.
questions.answer: Je parle français, mais je ne parle pas espagnol.
solution: Use parle with the first-person singular subject.
Use mais for the contrast and ne...pas around the second parle.
markingPoints: Write the correct negative Spanish clause.
